And she got help raising me from my grandparents. My grandfather was a janitor, and my grandmother cleaned homes. And when daycare was too expensive, she took me to work with her. So now I not only get to run to represent the same people whose homes, I watched my grandmother clean growing up. But when people like Elizabeth Warren talk about the need for universal childcare in this country, that is a fight that I want to join based on not wanting anyone to have to go through what I went through when I was growing up. You know, being gay and black, on top of those working-class experiences that I just described, make me acutely aware of what it's like to live in a society where at least for most of my life and for most of the life of other people in this country, gay people were not protected under our federal anti-discrimination law. Of course, we need a statute that clarifies that.
